methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $54M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DeepDrive is a Series B-stage transportation company that has raised $54.4M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 7 private frontier-transportation firms (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, The ePlane Company, and others), with no public comps available. The narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier proved insufficient for reliable median-based valuation.

Stage-progression analysis, the applicable method here, applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $54.4M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $103M. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics between Series B and later-stage financing in frontier transportation. No peer-median approach could be responsibly applied given the absence of three or more comparable datapoints within the same stage and tier; a broader sector median would conflate heterogeneous risk profiles and capital requirements.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M to $119M, with $103M as the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the adequacy of the 1.9x step-up multiplier for DeepDrive's specific risk profile and market position relative to undisclosed peer metrics. The single-method triangulation also leaves material sensitivity to stage-specific financing dynamics. Additional datapoints on comparable Series B closings in adjacent transportation subsectors would strengthen conviction.
